claude.sample_unit: patient education questions (12 LLMs x 4 setups); 50 PEMs for validation agent test

links.outcome: PEM generation quality with vs without RAG grounding across 12 LLMs
links.effect: ARAG-enabled setups (3 and 4) yielded the highest scores for 10 of the 12 models; ARAG positively contributed for most models.
links.quote: Based on the resulting scores, the top 5 experiments were identified.

links.outcome: Validation agent accuracy in blocking harmful patient education content
links.effect: Accuracy correlated with model size; Gemma-2-27b 0.82, Qwen2.5-32b 0.80; models <14B generally <0.50; Jais and Fanar 0.40 (blocked none); top performers failed on category 3 harmful PEMs.
links.quote: Models under 14B parameters generally scored below 0.50 accuracy, whereas only those with ≥27B parameters exceeded 0.80, suggesting sufficient parameter capacity is needed for reliable content validation in PE workflows.

links.outcome: LLM validation agent blocking of harmful generated PEMs
links.effect: Accuracy 0.40-0.82 across 12 LLMs; only models ≥27B exceeded 0.80; even top performers failed to dependably block category 3 unscientific advice.
links.quote: It is noteworthy that the full results from the VA evaluation ( online supplemental results , sheet ‘VA Eval’) show that even the top performers failed to dependably block harmful PEMs belonging to category 3 (unscientific or time-wasting medical advice).

links.outcome: Agreement between automated LLM evaluator ranking and blinded expert ranking of top configurations
links.effect: Expert ranking exactly matched automated ranking for the top five configurations, though absolute scores differed, largely in general medicine.
links.quote: A key finding was the exact match between the expert ranking and the automated ranking for these top five configurations.

links.outcome: Language adherence and consistency of outputs across setups
links.effect: Several models occasionally produced non-Arabic text despite Arabic-only inputs and RAG context; Jais-family-13b ranks ranged from 8th to 47th across setups.
links.quote: Despite receiving Arabic-only inputs and RAG context, several models (eg, Qwen-7b/32b, Gemma-2-27b, Jais-family-13b) occasionally produced non-Arabic text.

unlisted_practices: Using language-specific (Arabic-centred) LLMs for non-English patient education generation
Language validation rule scoring non-Arabic output as zero
Sentence-wise chunking and embedding model selection for RAG

links.effect: ARAG setups had highest scores for 10/12 models; AceGPT-v2-32B setup 4 ranked first with 4.69 automated and 4.32 expert overall.
links.quote: Results, detailed in table 1 , indicated a performance trend favouring ARAG-enabled setups (setups 3 and 4), which yielded the highest scores for 10 of the 12 models.

links.effect: Accuracy ranged from 0.40 (Jais variants, Fanar-S-1-7B) to 0.82 (Gemma-2-27b); even top performers failed to dependably block category 3 harmful PEMs.
links.quote: Top performers like ‘Gemma-2-27b’ (0.82 accuracy), ‘Qwen2.5-32b’ (0.80 accuracy) and ‘AceGPT-v2-32b’ (0.78 accuracy) reliably blocked harmful content from categories 1 and 2 (the most harmful PEMs), while smaller models including ‘Jais’ variants and ‘Fanar-S-1-7B’ performed poorly (0.40 accuracy).
